statements.t: There is no current public trading market for our common stock, and we do not expect that such a market will develop.
If we fail to continue to qualify as a REIT, our operations and distributions to stockholders will be adversely affected.

During the remainder of 2026, we intend to continue redeploying capital received from the repayment of legacy investments into newly originated loans and working with our current borrowers on extending or restructuring our maturing loans with an emphasis on obtaining principal reductions or loan payoffs.

Our ability to originate new loans and redeploy capital will continue to depend on conditions in the commercial real estate lending and capital markets, competition for lending opportunities, and other factors.

At the same time, our Board and management are evaluating a range of strategic options intended to maximize stockholder value and potentially provide our investors with access to some level of liquidity.
In connection with these efforts, management and the Board intend to engage an investment bank to assist in evaluating the strategic options available to the Company.
There is also no assurance that the Company will be able to successfully implement any strategic option.
We expect to complete the sale of the property in the fourth quarter of 2026.
We believe that excluding the amortization of premiums and discounts provides better insight to the expected contractual cash flows.
Neither FFO nor MFFO is intended to be an alternative to “net income” or to “cash flows from operating activities” as determined by GAAP as a measure of our capacity to pay distributions.

The calculation of our NAV is intended to be a calculation of the value of our assets less our outstanding liabilities for the purpose of establishing a purchase and repurchase price for our shares of common stock and may differ from our financial statements.
We will promptly disclose any changes to the identity or role of the independent valuation advisor in reports we publicly file with the SEC.
The majority of our investments consist of CRE loans intended to be held to maturity.
Since 2023, we have been required under GAAP to record a CECL reserve on the CRE debt portfolio that will be adjusted at least quarterly.

We believe this methodology is consistent with institutional valuation practices and provides an appropriate valuation for purposes of establishing a purchase and repurchase price for our shares of common stock as it relates to assets that are intended to be held to maturity.

We rely on property-level information provided by our Advisor, including but not limited to (1) historical and projected operating revenues and expenses of the property, (2) lease agreements with respect to the property and (3) information regarding recent or planned capital expenditures.
Each individual appraisal report for our assets will be addressed solely to our Company to assist in providing our monthly portfolio valuation.
Our aggregate monthly NAV will be reduced to reflect the accrual of the liability to pay any declared (and unpaid) distributions for all classes of common stock.

The reduction is intended to more closely align distributions with portfolio earnings, preserve capital and enhance our financial flexibility, including our ability to redeploy capital into new investments and evaluate potential strategic options.

The increase in the dividend rate on our Series A Preferred Stock from 6.75% per annum to 8.00% per annum (as discussed below under “Series A Preferred Stock”) is expected to increase our annual cash requirements for preferred stock dividends by approximately $1.1 million, based on the number of shares outstanding as of September 30, 2026.

We have an uncommitted master repurchase agreement (the “JPM Repo Facility”) with JPMorgan Chase Bank, National Association with a maximum facility amount of $526,076 that we expect to use to finance the acquisition or origination of eligible loans and participation interests therein.
If the underlying mortgage is in default, we will have the option to purchase the third party’s participation interest and remove it from the loan participation agreement.

We employed quarterly updated macroeconomic forecasts, which reflect expectations for overall economic output, interest rates, values of real estate properties and other factors, geopolitical instability and the Federal Reserve monetary policy impact on the overall U.S. economy and commercial real estate markets generally.

These estimates may change in future periods based on available future macroeconomic data and might result in a material change in our future estimates of expected credit losses for our loan portfolio.

We consider loan investments that are both (i) expected to be substantially repaid through the operation or sale of the underlying collateral, and (ii) for which the borrower is experiencing financial difficulty, to be “collateral-dependent” loans.

For loans that we determine foreclosure of the collateral is probable, we measure the expected losses based on the difference between the fair value of the collateral and the amortized cost basis of the loan as of the measurement date.

For collateral-dependent loans that we determine foreclosure is not probable, we apply a practical expedient to estimate expected losses using the difference between the collateral’s fair value (less costs to sell the asset if repayment is expected through the sale of the collateral) and the amortized cost basis of the loan.

All loans held-for-investment within our portfolio have some amount of expected loss to reflect the GAAP principal underlying the CECL model that all loans have some inherent risk of loss, regardless of credit quality, subordinate capital or other mitigating factors.
The allowance for credit losses is estimated on a quarterly basis and represents management’s estimates of current expected credit losses in our investment portfolio.

We license certain macroeconomic financial forecasts from a third-party to inform our view of the potential future impact that broader macroeconomic conditions may have on the performance of the loans held-for-investment.
We may use one or more of these forecasts in the process of estimating our allowance for credit losses.

Selection of these economic forecasts requires significant judgment about future events that, while based on the information available to us as of the balance sheet date, are ultimately unknowable with certainty, and the actual economic conditions impacting our portfolio could vary significantly from the estimates we made for the periods presented.

Significant inputs to our estimate of the allowance for credit losses include the reasonable and supportable forecast period and loan specific factors such as debt service coverage ratio, or DSCR, loan-to-value ratio (“LTV”), remaining contractual loan term, property type and others.
We will provide without charge a copy of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q upon written request delivered to our principal executive offices.
